Neutral Citation No. - 2023:AHC:146097 Court No. - 4 Case :- APPLICATION U/S 482 No. - 26113 of 2023 Applicant :- Sharafat And 3 Others Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another Counsel for Applicant :- Sanjay Kr. Srivastava Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Prakash Padia,J.

1. Heard learned counsel for the applicants and learned A.G.A. for the State.
2.

The present 482 Cr.P.C. application has been filed to quash the charge sheet dated 16.2.2018,
summoning order dated 28.6.2018 as well as the entire proceedings of Case No. 42479 of 2018 (New Case No.4112 of 2020) (State Vs. Sharafat and others), arising out of Case Crime No. 61 of 2017,
under Sections- 498A, 504, 506, 323, 325 I.P.C., Section- 3/4 of D.P. Act, Police Station- Mahila Thana, District- Meerut, pending in the court of Civil Judge (J.D.) FTC (Crime Against Women),
Meerut.

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for the applicants submits that the present dispute arises out of matrimonial discord between the applicants and the opposite party no. 2.

The present criminal case has been lodged against the applicant no.1 (husband) and his other family members but that no real criminal offence had actually occurred.
4.
It is thus submitted that the present criminal prosecution has been lodged by the opposite party no. 2 owing to some misunderstanding and misgivings between the parties.
With passage of time they have been able to resolve their differences.
The parties are living together in matrimony and in the changed circumstance, the opposite party no. 2 does not wish to press charges against the present applicants.

In fact, it is submitted that if the criminal prosecution is allowed to proceed it may create further complication in the otherwise normal relationship i.e. arising between the estranged couple and their families.
5. He further submits, at present, the opposite party no. 2 does not wish to press charge against the applicants.
6. Sri Ayush Srivastava, learned counsel for the opposite party no. 2 does not dispute the correctness of the submission made by learned counsel for the applicants.
In fact, in this regard opposite party no.2 has filed counter affidavit, and in paragraph no.4 of the same the opposite party no.2 has stated about the compromise dated 28.3.2023.
The opposite party no. 2, has supported the contention advanced by learned counsel for the applicants.

7. Accordingly, it is provided that the parties shall appear before the court below and file a certified copy of this order within two weeks, along with the original copy of the compromise dated 28.3.2023.

It is, therefore, expected that the court below may fix a date for the verification of the compromise entered into between the parties and pass an appropriate order to that effect within next four weeks.
8. In view of the above, the present application is disposed of.
9. For a period of two months or till the final order passed on the compromise application by the court below whichever is earlier, no coercive measure shall be taken against the applicant.
10. In case, the applicants are still aggrieved or if no action is taken, it will be open for the applicant to approach this Court afresh.

Order Date :- 21.7.2023 S.K.
